newsitem.title: USA: Dutchman reads toes for clues to personality.
newsitem.headline: Dutchman reads toes for clues to personality.

text.p: Take off your shoes and socks in front of Imre Somogyi and you may get an earful.
The Netherlands native reads peoples' toes for insights into their personalities. He is, by his own estimation, the world's first toe reader.

"Working with feet, you can tell something about a person's character or how they behave," he said in an interview Saturday at BookExpo America, where he was promoting his book, "Reading Toes: Your Feet as Reflections of Your Personality."
At the show, Somogyi read the toes of Melissa Parsons of New York City and told her that the inward turn of her right small toe reflected a tendency "to turn away from the subject."

Asked if perhaps her shoes might simply be too tight, Somogyi said, "Accepting shoes that hurt your feet does tell you something about someone's willingness to submit themselves to what some idiot in Italy says about fashion."
Somogyi has formed the Foundation for Fundamental Dactylogical Reading. He has a software package on toe reading, along with the book, and he spends much time teaching others to read toes.
Ninety percent of his students and 70 percent of those who come to him for readings are women. "Women are very open. Men hide their toes," he said.
He reads the toes by looking at them and making observations about their shape, size and surface. He told Parsons that the ridges on her toenails showed she had volatile emotions.
"He was pretty accurate on some of the things he said about me," the young woman said after her session.

She said she was reading Somogyi's book but found it occasionally inconvenient, especially on her lunch hour. "You have to read it with your shoes off and restaurants in Manhattan frown on that," she said.
